steps.content: Starting with a Random Forest model with 100 trees and a maximum depth of 10 should provide a good balance between bias and variance, allowing for effective learning from the training data.

The Random Forest model with 100 trees and a maximum depth of 10 achieved a validation accuracy of 0.94737, indicating strong performance. The mean cross-validation accuracy is also high at 0.96478, suggesting good generalization. I will refine this configuration to search for an even better performance.
Increasing the number of trees to 150 while keeping the maximum depth at 10 may enhance the model's ability to capture more complexity in the data without overfitting.

The updated Random Forest model with 150 trees and a maximum depth of 10 has improved the validation accuracy to 0.95322, which is better than the previous configuration. Given this positive result, I will continue refining to see if further improvements can be achieved.
Increasing the maximum depth to 12 while maintaining 150 trees might allow the model to learn even more complex patterns in the data without significantly increasing overfitting risk.

The Random Forest model with 150 trees and a maximum depth of 12 did not improve upon the validation accuracy of 0.95322 achieved with the previous configuration. Given that further refinements in this direction have yielded no gains, I will stop here.

steps.final_recommendation: I recommend using the Random Forest model with 150 trees and a maximum depth of 10, as it achieved the highest validation accuracy of 0.95322 and demonstrates good generalization performance.
